![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14218806/assets/11e1c9a550944fc8435fc0d6f17be7d172e0c6d8f82fc1af950896f6ec8176b6.png)

Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above?  

I. ${lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x)=1$

III. ${lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's look at each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. As $x$ approaches $0$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$  approaches $y=1.$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{+}}f(x)=1.
$$

- Statement II is true. As $x$ approaches $2$ from the left, the function value $f(x)$ approaches $y=1$, Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x)=1.
$$

- Statement III is false. As $x$ approaches $-1$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$ is undefined. Consequently,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

Instead, as $x$ approaches $-1$ from the left, the function value $f(x)$ approaches $y=1$, and consequently

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)=1.
$$

 Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x).
$$

Therefore, only statement II is true.
